title: What if you fell into Jupiter? 🪐
subject: jupiter
description:
How far down do you think you'd get? 👇

Jupiter has no solid surface. NASA's Galileo probe dropped into it in 1995 at 106,000 mph and lasted 58 minutes before the pressure and heat silenced it. Here's what that fall would do to you.

Sources: NASA Science ("Jupiter Facts"), NASA Science ("Galileo Jupiter Atmospheric Probe"), NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory
tags: what if you fell into jupiter

scenes.text: If you fell into Jupiter, you'd never land.
There's no ground, just gas getting thicker and hotter as you sink.
NASA's Galileo probe tried it on December 7, 1995, hitting the clouds at 106,000 miles per hour.
On the way down it measured winds of half a mile per second.
It sent data for 58 minutes, fell about 112 miles, and went silent at 22 times Earth's air pressure.
Far deeper, hydrogen gets squeezed into liquid metal. You'd be crushed long before you saw it.
